q1_longest_experiments: The arXiv Bundle v10 task consumed 10 of 16 minutes (62.5%). Root cause: the gate dependency on Exp 1269 (arXiv critical fixes) has not been cleared across eight consecutive milestones (.99 through .108). Each milestone relaunches the bundle task, which spends ~10 min discovering the gate is still blocked before emitting a terminal artifact. The correct fix is an activation-time gate preflight that emits the GATE_BLOCKED terminal artifact in <1 s without spinning up the full experiment.
q2_gpu_utilization: Both RTX 3090s are idle at 4 MB / 0% utilization (GPU 0: 50C, GPU 1: 54C). No GPU-bearing experiments were scheduled in this closeout-only milestone. DualGPURunner was not used. The 16-min wall time was entirely CPU and conductor overhead. GPUs have been idle at closeout for at least eight consecutive milestones.
q3_zombie_processes: No zombie GPU processes observed. Both GPUs show 4 MB allocated but 0% utilization, consistent with the driver baseline rather than a leaked process. The gpu_monitor.py advisory suggestions (free memory, use DualGPURunner) are not indicators of active leaks in this closeout slice.
q4_parallelization: All five experiments ran sequentially. The arXiv bundle gate and three SOTA GGUF doomed-rerun blocks are structurally sequential (each must discover it is blocked before the next launches). True parallelization is only applicable to GPU-bearing research experiments in non-closeout milestones. For this closeout slice, the correct optimization is not parallelism but activation-time gate/doomed-rerun checks that skip blocked tasks in <1 s rather than running them for 2-10 min each.
q5_preflight_bottleneck: Preflight tests are not a bottleneck in this slice. Adjacent-milestone conductor logs show test suites completing in 5-26 seconds. The 16-min wall time is dominated by gate-blocked tasks, not test suite execution.
q6_doc_reconciliation: Doc reconciliation registered 0 min for the in-process docs task (matched the parent's gate-blocked outcome instantly). Not a bottleneck. The deferred-docs concern from prior retros does not apply to this closeout slice.
q7_tooling_improvements: The same three improvements have been recommended for eight consecutive milestones without mechanical enforcement: (1) activation-time gate/DOOMED_RERUN checks emitting immediate terminal blocked artifacts; (2) retirement of SOTA GGUF cache gate task after first block within a milestone; (3) resolution of Exp 1269 upstream to clear the arXiv publication path. The retro feedback loop is structurally broken — recommendations are generated but not mechanically enforced by the conductor.

Three duplicate DOOMED_RERUN_BLOCK slots for SOTA GGUF: 6 min / 37.5% of wall time — conductor should retire after first block within a milestone, not relaunch twice more
Stale retro feedback loop: same improvements estimated at 30-35% for eight consecutive retros (.99 through .108) without mechanical enforcement in the conductor
No GPU experiments scheduled in closeout-only milestones: both RTX 3090s idle at 4 MB / 0% throughout 16 min
Exp 1269 upstream critical fix has blocked arXiv publication path for 8+ milestones — the fix itself is the load-bearing unresolved item
improvements_suggested: Activation-time gate preflight: before launching any gated experiment, check if the gate condition is already known-false in prior artifacts and emit an immediate terminal GATE_BLOCKED artifact (<1 s vs current 10 min discovery cost)

Single-shot doomed-rerun retirement: when a task receives a DOOMED_RERUN_BLOCK verdict, add it to the exclusion manifest for the remainder of the current milestone — do not launch the same task again 2 and 4 minutes later

Exp 1269 escalation gate: if Exp 1269 (arXiv critical fixes) has not produced a clearing artifact in N consecutive milestones, escalate to operator with a hard block rather than continuing to propose the downstream arXiv bundle
Retro-to-conductor mechanical enforcement: convert retro 'improvements_suggested' entries into conductor pre-launch checks that run automatically, not advisory text requiring planner re-reading
Schedule GPU-bearing research experiments in non-closeout milestones using DualGPURunner to break the 8-milestone GPU-idle streak at closeout time

Milestones .99 through .108 have produced the same retro findings and the same 30-35% savings estimate without mechanical remediation. The retro is no longer functioning as a discovery mechanism — it is a symptom tracker for a known-and-unresolved conductor design defect. Writing another identical retro report does not improve the situation. The only action that would change the .109 retro outcome is shipping the activation-time gate/doomed-rerun preflight as a conductor code change. Until that happens, this retro will correctly predict that milestone .109 produces the same artifact.
